b=s.index('   The preview must pass',a)
s=s[:a]+'''   Do not destroy runtime hosts from the canonical dev root with `-target`.
   Terraform's reverse dependency closure also selects retained configuration, ECS
   services, IAM bindings, publisher functions and database proxies. Scaling those
   consumers to zero does not remove their dependency edges. Instead, use a private
   local execution state containing only the exact approved runtime resources.
   The canonical backend keeps every resource and dependency; do not remove, import,
   push or restore any canonical state for this procedure.

   Run this on the existing authorized Terraform state runner, with applies paused
   for the entire window. It grants no human backend access or secret-read permission.
   Keep state files and saved plans on that runner only, under mode 0700/0600; they
   can contain secrets. Retain sanitized receipts, never state contents, as evidence.
   `prepare-reset` verifies the caller, every selected address/type/ID/ARN and the
   archive hold, filters retained consumers out of the execution copy, preserves
   ordering among approved resources, assigns a separate lineage and copies the
   dev root's locked AWS provider. Its empty configuration uses only a local backend.
   Existing lifecycle protections remain unchanged in tracked modules.

   ```bash
   umask 077
   aws --profile crpko-dev --region ap-south-1 sts get-caller-identity > tmp/dev-reset-caller.json
   AWS_PROFILE=crpko-dev AWS_REGION=ap-south-1 terraform -chdir=terraform/roots/dev state pull > tmp/dev-canonical-state.json
   node scripts/runbooks/dev-rebuild-operation.mjs prepare-reset --scope tmp/dev-rebuild-scope.json --operation tmp/dev-rebuild-operation.json --state tmp/dev-canonical-state.json --caller tmp/dev-reset-caller.json --writer-evidence tmp/dev-archive-writers.json --output tmp/dev-runtime-reset
   terraform -chdir=tmp/dev-runtime-reset init -input=false -lockfile=readonly
   AWS_PROFILE=crpko-dev AWS_REGION=ap-south-1 terraform -chdir=tmp/dev-runtime-reset plan -destroy -input=false -out=reset.tfplan
   terraform -chdir=tmp/dev-runtime-reset show -json reset.tfplan > tmp/dev-runtime-reset.tfplan.json
   node --input-type=module <<'JS'
   import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
   import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
   const read = path => JSON.parse(readFileSync(path));
   const scope = read('tmp/dev-rebuild-scope.json');
   const caller = read('tmp/dev-reset-caller.json');
   const plan = read('tmp/dev-runtime-reset.tfplan.json');
   if (caller.Account !== scope.account) throw new Error('wrong reset account');
   writeFileSync('tmp/dev-reset-target.json', JSON.stringify({
     account: caller.Account, caller_arn: caller.Arn, region: scope.region,
     source_revision: scope.source_revision,
     plan_sha256: createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(plan)).digest('hex')
   }), {mode: 0o600});
   JS
   node scripts/runbooks/dev-rebuild-operation.mjs check-reset --scope tmp/dev-rebuild-scope.json --operation tmp/dev-rebuild-operation.json --state tmp/dev-canonical-state.json --output tmp/dev-runtime-reset --input tmp/dev-runtime-reset.tfplan.json --target-evidence tmp/dev-reset-target.json --writer-evidence tmp/dev-archive-writers.json
   ```

   S3 cleanup is prefix-scoped and never uses
   `runbook:purge-dev-s3-bucket-versions --full-teardown`; that older utility includes
   evidence. The execution copy is a temporary, explicitly scoped teardown path;
   it is never used for provisioning or routine deployments.

'''+s[b:]
a=s.index('4. After the archive decommission')
b=s.index('   After recreation and before any baseline/producer',a)
s=s[:a]+'''4. After archive decommission, repeat the runtime plan, target attestation and
   guard above with fresh ECS/task/broker readbacks, retaining the pre-deletion upload
   drain response and bucket-deletion receipt. Do not query uploads on a deleted
   bucket. Pull canonical state again into `tmp/dev-canonical-current.json` and pass
   it to `check-reset --state` in place of the earlier snapshot. Any change, including
   its lineage or serial, stops execution. All applies must still be paused. Inspect
   the complete plan and archive receipts, then apply exactly that saved local plan:

   ```bash
   AWS_PROFILE=crpko-dev AWS_REGION=ap-south-1 terraform -chdir=terraform/roots/dev state pull > tmp/dev-canonical-current.json
   node scripts/runbooks/dev-rebuild-operation.mjs check-reset --scope tmp/dev-rebuild-scope.json --operation tmp/dev-rebuild-operation.json --state tmp/dev-canonical-current.json --output tmp/dev-runtime-reset --input tmp/dev-runtime-reset.tfplan.json --target-evidence tmp/dev-reset-target.json --writer-evidence tmp/dev-archive-writers.json
   AWS_PROFILE=crpko-dev AWS_REGION=ap-south-1 terraform -chdir=tmp/dev-runtime-reset apply -input=false reset.tfplan
   ```

   This replaces FDB/ClickHouse/Kafka's complete approved host/data-volume cohorts,
   Redis's whole replication group and exact Registry/queue/stream runtime resources.
   Canonical state stays intact; the subsequent normal canonical plan refreshes
   missing resources and recreates them from baseline. Never push execution state
   into the backend. Before that apply, inspect the full canonical plan and prove
   retained resources have no delete or replacement actions. Changed endpoint bindings
   may update retained consumers, which remain stopped until their bootstrap gates.

   **Aurora and Mathesar:** retain clusters, instances, proxies and their configuration
   and secrets. RDS deletes a managed master secret when its cluster is deleted, so
   physical cluster replacement violates the retained-secret boundary and the guard
   refuses it. Reset each approved application database on its existing writer instead.
   Inventory every database on every control/shard/Mathesar server, including identical
   database names on different hosts, against the service release configuration.
   Add one `database_resets` record per database to the approved scope with unique `id`,
   exact writer `host`, `port`, `database`, `owner`, `admin_user`, `encoding`, `collate`,
   `ctype` and `locale_provider` from `pg_database`. Keep maintenance/template databases
   and global roles. Missing databases, unknown owners, unsupported locale providers or
   prepared transactions stop the reset. Final backups and the writer hold still apply.

   On the existing VPC PostgreSQL administration runner, use the already-authorized
   administrative connection and private password file with RDS CA verification.
   Do not add task roles, read or print secret values, or use a proxy for this operation.
   For each approved ID, generate the SQL before execution:

   ```bash
   node scripts/runbooks/dev-rebuild-operation.mjs postgres-reset-sql --scope tmp/dev-rebuild-scope.json --operation tmp/dev-rebuild-operation.json --database "$database_id" --writer-evidence tmp/dev-archive-writers.json --output "tmp/dev-reset-postgres-$database_id.sql"
   ```

   Bind `PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, `PGUSER` to that record, `PGDATABASE=postgres`,
   `PGSSLMODE=verify-full`, and `PGSSLROOTCERT`/`PGPASSFILE` to the existing private
   runner files. Inspect the generated SQL, then run
   `psql -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f "tmp/dev-reset-postgres-$database_id.sql"`.
   It checks the exact current database metadata and administrator before dropping
   that database with FORCE and recreating it from template0 with its existing owner,
   encoding and libc locale. No role/password is recreated or rotated. A nonzero or
   interrupted execution is unknown: read `pg_database` and the database's relations
   before reconciling the journal; never blindly rerun the drop. No seed or baseline
   may start until every approved database has an empty user-relation readback.

'''+s[b:]
a=s.index('5. Remove `terraform/roots/dev/dev-archive-teardown_override.tf`')
b=s.index('\nAfter the first destructive step',a)
s=s[:a]+'''5. Remove `terraform/roots/dev/dev-archive-teardown_override.tf` and the local
   `tmp/dev-archive-teardown-module` copy, reinitialize the dev root and verify the
   shared archive module still has all three normal lifecycle guards. Verify the
   approved source diff is empty, including the normal data-volume and Redis lifecycle
   guards. No execution-copy state or temporary unlock may enter a normal rebuild.
   Record source, plan and applied settings separately. Keep private execution receipts
   through reconciliation, then dispose of the local state/plan copies under the
   runner's existing secret-handling policy. Never delete canonical state or backups.
   Read every reset store back empty, including the full FoundationDB keyspace,
   Aurora/Mathesar application databases, ClickHouse and Keeper, Kafka/KRaft, Redis,
   Registry, queues/streams and runtime prefixes. Stop on residual data. Record the
   empty-state proof before native genesis; no old-state restore is part of this reset.
'''+s[b:]
s=s.replace('The guard admits these named dependents only\n   with a host or the matching cache-volume deletion in the same cohort;', 'The guard admits these named dependents only\n   with a host or the matching cache-volume deletion in the same cohort;')
s=s.replace('requires the same input and a running teardown step; `check-plan` requires fresh','requires the same input and a running teardown step. `prepare-reset` creates only a\nprivate local execution state, and `check-reset` binds its exact plan to unchanged\ncanonical state and the approved scope. PostgreSQL SQL generation selects one unique\napproved database ID. `check-plan` requires fresh')
p.write_text(s)
p=Path('README.md');s=p.read_text().replace('Terraform dependency closure. Offline operation checks:', 'runtime-only execution state that leaves the canonical backend intact. Aurora and\nMathesar database contents reset in place so managed master secrets survive. Offline operation checks:');p.write_text(s)
PY

# Holder release cancellation repair

Repository: Equicom-Crypto/crpko-integration-harness. Base native-v1 f5f8246cba6fe63935b7a0550a41f31825564b99, including dependency PR 530. Commit b04edd170e0c33ab832e3cf094dc766e6a80a149, branch fix/holder-release-3750. Three tracked files, 236 insertions and 5 deletions. PR pending full-suite acceptance.

## Resulting behavior

A non-gateway hold decrements its holder count synchronously once before acquiring the condition to notify waiters. Cancellation while acquiring is deferred through retries. Known stale proof is invalidated for the same evidence before cancellation propagates. Only the exception actually leaving the hold is preserved; an already-handled outer exception cannot suppress cancellation. The executor passes its actual body exception into non-gateway exits, so a cancelled body skips the successful-body AppConfig proof. Gateway's exit call and its branch behavior are retained. Evidence construction is covered by the armed try/finally.

## Regression proof

All eight cases fail original production code from f5f8246c in a separate ovnfs checkout, copying only the new test file; old-all-regressions.log: 8 failed, 5 deselected, exit 1.

| Case | Baseline failure | Corrected behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AppConfig contended exit | holders remains 1 | holders 0, next different fault restores/stages |
| ECS contended exit | holders remains 1 | same exact release and progress |
| Stale-proof reacquire | same evidence remains ready | ready false, holders 0 |
| Double cancel | second cancel rejected after premature exit | both accepted, first object propagates, count 2 |
| Body ValueError | replaced by cleanup cancellation | same ValueError object |
| Body CancelledError | replaced by cleanup cancellation | same CancelledError object |
| Successful hold inside handled exception | baseline leaks count; first candidate suppressed cancellation | cancellation propagates, count released |
| Real executor body cancellation | second cancel in post-body proof replaces original | same original cancellation; no post-body proof |

Events gate all interleavings. Only the explicitly requested sleep(0) between double cancels is used. The AppConfig sibling blocks naturally in serving_changed under the condition. ECS reuse has no such provider await; that sibling is paused at its entry condition boundary to exercise the same real holder-exit path. Each corrected case also checks original exception identity and Task.cancelling count where relevant, release to zero and subsequent restore/stage under a five-second bound.

The independent first check exposed the ambient-exception issue and pre-existing executor caller gap. exceptions.qnt was added before correcting those paths; new regressions fail the first candidate in first-candidate-exception-fails.log. The subsequent independent check is clear; INDEPENDENT-CHECK.md records it. Its cancellation probe independently passed all 13 cases.

## Commands and local results

Run from /Users/ardud/checkouts/harness-holder-release-3750, with PYTHONPATH=src:tests and Python /Users/ardud/CrpkoArchitectureBroker/tmp/crpko-integration-harness/.venv/bin/python (3.12).

- Baseline checkout: `python -m pytest -q tests/test_fault_cancellation.py -k 'holder or executor_preserves'`: 8 failed, 5 deselected, exit 1. old-all-regressions.log.
- First candidate: `python -m pytest -q tests/test_fault_cancellation.py -k 'inside_handled_exception or executor_preserves'`: 2 failed, 11 deselected, exit 1. first-candidate-exception-fails.log.
- Corrected candidate: `python -m pytest -q tests/test_fault_cancellation.py`: 13 passed, exit 0. final-cancellation.log.
- Each of the remaining nine tests/test_*fault*.py files individually with `python -m pytest -q <file>`: all passed. final-test_*.log. Total across all ten requested modules: 374 passed; one existing collection warning, zero thread/unraisable warnings.
- `python -m pytest -q tests/test_executor_expectations.py`: 104 passed, one existing collection warning, exit 0. final-executor-expectations.log.
- `git diff --check`: exit 0. Checked index tree recorded in checked-index-tree.txt; commit tree matches it. Candidate files match candidate-files.sha256.

## Quint

Canonical files: quint/holders.qnt and quint/exceptions.qnt. Invariants, abstraction limits, counterexamples, commands and exit codes: MODEL-REPORT.md and quint/COMMANDS.md. Model files stay outside the PR.

Holder model: exact count, release/notify before return, stale-proof invalidation, original exception token and unchanged cancellation request count. Old release/wakeup/stale/outcome variants fail. Separate old trace has holders=0 and ready=true with stale debt, proving invalidation can fail independently of count release. Fixed normal and contended simulations each pass 10,000 schedules, fixed depth-8 bounded checks pass.

Exception model: ambient handled exception versus actual escaping body exception and manual executor exit. Both buggy steps fail simulation and bounded verification. Fixed simulation passes 10,000 schedules and bounded verification passes depth 8. All verification runs under 20 minutes, on unique port 9550, with Java 21+. Servers stopped. No unbounded progress is claimed if a provider holds the condition forever or scheduling is unfair.

## Sibling and caller audit

- faults.py hold's proof_stale condition block and holder-exit condition block: both repaired.
- faults.py EcsInjector._mutate finally: completed-future discard is synchronous; no cleanup condition acquire.
- faults.py GatewayInjector.install except and hold gateway finally: shielded remove, no holder counter or condition acquire; retained.
- faults.py stage finally: existing cancellation-draining SDK path then synchronous fd close; no async condition acquire.
- faults.py phase finally: synchronous fd close.
- appconfig_faults.py _mutate finally: synchronous completed-future discard; no async lock/condition block in this file.
- completion/fault_restore.py store initialization and database finally: synchronous close. recovery_scope and SDK transport context finally: synchronous ContextVar resets. lock_fault exception: synchronous fd close. recover_fault finally: existing cancellation-draining SDK path then synchronous fd close. No async lock/condition blocks in this file.
- executor.py is the only production hold caller: now forwards the actual escaping body exception for non-gateway exits. No other manual hold exit call sites found.

Harness skill and wiki guidance checked: deterministic fault cleanup, original cancellation, strict warning policy, native-v1 target and its exact-head merge loop agree. No architecture contract, provider credentials, service repository, live configuration, deploy, skill or watcher changes are required. No R4 source/lease changes or PR 526 work.

cat > docs/TORCORE_VERIFICATION.md <<'EOF'
# Tor core packet verification

This is harness preparation for card #10, not a Tor privacy or release sign-off.
The scenarios needing embedded Tor, bridges and Orbot remain pending their
implementation cards. No real client hosts are used.

## Capture method

The standalone synthetic debug APK in `torcore/verify/capture/` uses Android's
`VpnService`. It routes IPv4 and IPv6 into a TUN interface and forwards raw IP
packets through one protected UDP socket to a dedicated disposable Linux VM.
The VM injects them into a Linux TUN interface and uses kernel routing/NAT for
replies. Android retains its own TCP stack; there is no test TCP reimplementation.
The gateway records outgoing inner IP packets in classic raw-IP pcap, with
packet-indexed UID records from Android's `getConnectionOwnerUid` where available.
Only the tunnel socket is protected from the VPN. The VM is the #3 throwaway
host, never a client host. It must stay reserved until collection and be deleted.

The APK is a separate SDK-only build, outside every Gradle application/library
source set. It has no release build. Release pre-R8 classes, original/inlined
R8 origins, final dex and manifest audits reject its package/markers/components.
`check.sh` builds the standalone debug APK without runtime configuration. A
configured lab APK contains an ephemeral tunnel token: keep it private and
remove its cloud asset after testing. The token authenticates only this disposable
synthetic tunnel; it is sent in clear and is not a production VPN protocol.

On the shared Nothing phone, scope is restricted to the synthetic capture APK.
Personal apps are not added to the VPN. A clean cloud session uses `scope=all`
(no per-app allowlist), with only system networking, the sample and the capture
fixture installed. Orbot must run in SOCKS mode: Android supports one VPN, so
Orbot VPN mode cannot be measured with this collector.

### Limits and effects

- This observes app IP packets routed through the VPN, not a physical-interface
  wire tap. Loopback/Unix sockets, the protected tunnel socket, privileged
  networking that bypasses the VPN and another VPN are outside its observation.
  Do not describe it as an independent proof of every physical-interface packet.
- Routing, source addresses, DNS configuration, MTU (1280) and public egress change.
  The configured DNS server deliberately makes plaintext DNS visible; it is not
  a Tor setting. Connectivity checks may add system traffic. A baseline records
  that traffic; it must not silently exempt DNS or non-relay traffic in later rows.
- UID is an Android-reported socket owner, not a PID. Embedded Tor and the sample
  share a UID. A post-transition packet with that shared UID cannot by itself
  prove Tor owned the connection. Those cases need process/socket evidence in
  #10; the analyzer reports an inconclusive result instead of a pass.
- Unknown UID, missing packet coverage, a missing relay snapshot, sequence gaps,
  unavailable transitions, parser limitations or capture failure are evidence
  gaps. A blackhole tunnel and a silent/empty capture are not clean results.
- Device timestamps travel with packets; transition timestamps must use that
  same Android wall clock. Record monotonic transition timing too and reject
  clock changes. The gateway snapshot metadata brackets collector lifetime,
  not the sample's idle observation window.
- This method depends on an IPv6 path to the VM. Loss of that outer path can
  drop observations. Network-transition rows need a canary before and after
  each transition and gap accounting; a gap cannot pass fail-closed testing.
- Known resolver IPs catch some DoH, not arbitrary encrypted DNS. The analyzer
  does not decrypt TLS, infer hidden names or prove capture completeness.

## Method spike evidence (10 November 2026)

Current `runcloud` 0.2.0 help, the provider's complete docs and SDK 0.49.0
`SimulatorClient` surface expose no packet capture, pcap export, proxy, ADB or
shell. Screen/audio recording is unrelated. The attempted public `/changelog`
URL returned 404; no changelog evidence is claimed. The provider docs still
support only install, deep links, UI actions and retained logs for Android.
The SDK additionally exposes install-on-existing-session, used by the helper.

Physical phone: Nothing A001T, API 35, arm64-v8a. No root. Ordinary shell tools
expose aggregate netstats and some `/proc/net/tcp` socket snapshots; these cannot
capture packets, transient SYNs, DNS questions or complete IPv6/UDP attempts.
They are complementary evidence only.

The synthetic seed sent one explicit UDP DNS query for `example.com` to a numeric
resolver and one TCP connect to port 22 on the fixture VM's public IPv6 address.
The gateway pcap contained **15 outbound packets, 2 DNS/53 packets and 1 public-IP
TCP SYN**. The app received a **61-byte DNS reply**, proving forwarding rather
than a VPN that only consumes packets. The closed public port rejected the TCP
attempt as expected: the onion host's SSH stays on loopback.

Private pcap SHA-256:
`30ab7e3f864a6ae8762306cb4f80d72068ab8760c31345a665ebb1968f80880a`.
No pcap, public fixture address, onion, key or tunnel token is committed. This
first spike predates UID framing; it establishes packet visibility, not UID
coverage. The synthetic APK was stopped and uninstalled from the phone. The
initial VM's onion/SSH state was erased (`port_22=closed`), the gateway was killed,
and `offbox release bx_jbw5gxm2 --delete` confirmed deletion.

All-app cloud proof and the 60-second sample-Off baseline are still pending.
No baseline pass is claimed here until their actual evidence is recorded.

## Analyzer and self-test

`python3 -m unittest discover -s torcore/verify -p 'test_analyze.py'` runs from
`check.sh`. Fixtures are generated in memory/temporary directories, not stored
pcaps. Each seeded leak is checked independently: DNS, direct-to-fixture SYN,
embedded non-relay connection and unowned post-transition connection. Clean
fixtures must pass; malformed, truncated, unsupported or unattributed evidence
must not pass. Both pcap byte orders and pcapng are covered.

Use `python3 torcore/verify/analyze.py --help` for the exact CLI and UID/exception
schemas. Exit 0 is pass within the supplied capture scope, 1 is an observed
violation, and 2 is inconclusive. Preserve the exit code, report and evidence
hashes. Supply the fixture's public IPv4/IPv6 addresses independently, never an
onion. Supply consensus/GETINFO `ns/all` data from the Tor instance already
running; no live network lookup is performed by the analyzer. Bridge input is
numeric IPs only. Snowflake exemptions require exact documented DNS questions,
broker endpoints and valid STUN messages; no blanket DNS/HTTPS allowance.

## Row procedure for #10

`bash torcore/verify/run-matrix.sh --plan` lists every row and dependency. The
script is an explicit skeleton; pending rows do not execute or return a pass.

1. Generate the throwaway keys with `testhost/keys.sh`. Run `run-matrix.sh --host`
   with the public-key argument from `testhost/README.md` in an attached shell.
   Record its box/run IDs and wait for `CAPTURE_GATEWAY_READY`. Do not end the
   reservation while builds run: the fixture masks SSH, so only Boat API works.
2. `collect.py configure BOX tmp/verify/config.properties --scope all` privately
   saves that VM's endpoint/token. `run-matrix.sh --build-capture CONFIG` builds
   offbox and pulls the configured APK. Keep all runtime files under ignored
   `tmp/`. Never publish the configured APK.
3. `run-matrix.sh --device APK` allocates through rcsim. Upload the sample APK
   with `runcloud asset push`, then use `cloud-install.py SESSION ASSET` to
   install it on that owned session. Install Orbot similarly for its rows only.
   Record every APK hash. Heartbeat at least every 15 minutes and release the
   session while waiting for long builds. Do not claim an API based on a label.
4. Open `torssh-debug://capture` and accept Android's real VPN consent. The
   capture log reports SDK, ABI, scope, capture UID and sample UID. Reach the
   sample via `torssh-debug://capture?action=sample`; verify its Off state for
   row 1. Run the seeded check with `run-matrix.sh --seed SESSION`. Confirm both
   seeded packet types and a DNS reply, not merely a success log.
5. Use a fresh collector/run per row (or implement and verify bounded slicing).
   Record the row start/end and any fail-closed transition on the packet clock.
   Run row 1 idle for at least 60 seconds. Run the sample's numeric/status debug
   actions for later rows once #7/#8/#9 expose them; do not invent deep-link
   handlers. `runcloud android logs` plus `filter-logs.py` retains allowlisted
   result lines only. Current sample has no scenario deep-link harness yet.
6. `collect.py snapshot BOX tmp/verify/ROW` requests an immutable pcap + bound UID
   sidecar + capture counts. Sequence gaps invalidate completeness. Analyze
   with the exact mode, device IPs `10.237.0.2` / `fd37:37::2`, fixture IPs,
   UID sets, relay/bridge snapshot and transition timestamp for that row. Record
   only redacted results/counts/hashes; pcaps are ignored by git.
7. Stop the VPN and release with `run-matrix.sh --release SESSION`. Delete any
   uploaded fixture assets. Stop the gateway/host reservation, confirm down.sh
   erased onion/SSH state, then `offbox release BOX --delete`. Verify `rcsim list`
   and VM deletion. Never save a snapshot of the fixture or its identities.

Rows 2–4 wait for #7/#8. Rows 5–7 wait for #9; SOCKS mode is measurable, VPN
mode is not. Rows 8–9 additionally need actual device controls and uninterrupted
observation across network changes. Rows 10–11 require process attribution for
shared-UID embedded traffic. Row 12 needs #7 plus the authenticated #3 host.
API 29, API 33 and live 16 KiB-page devices remain unavailable, as recorded in
wiki `device-testing`; this harness does not manufacture those passes.

embedded non-relay connection and unowned post-transition connection. Clean
fixtures must pass; malformed, truncated, unsupported or unattributed evidence
must not pass. Both pcap byte orders and pcapng are covered.

Use `python3 torcore/verify/analyze.py --help` for the exact CLI and UID/exception
schemas. Exit 0 is pass within the supplied capture scope, 1 is an observed
violation, and 2 is inconclusive. Preserve the exit code, report and evidence
hashes. Supply the fixture's public IPv4/IPv6 addresses independently, never an
onion. Supply consensus/GETINFO `ns/all` data from the Tor instance already
running; no live network lookup is performed by the analyzer. Bridge input is
numeric IPs only. Snowflake exemptions require exact documented DNS questions,
broker endpoints and valid STUN messages; no blanket DNS/HTTPS allowance.

## Row procedure for #10

`bash torcore/verify/run-matrix.sh --plan` lists every row and dependency. The
script is an explicit skeleton; pending rows do not execute or return a pass.

1. Generate the throwaway keys with `testhost/keys.sh`. Run `run-matrix.sh --host`
   with the public-key argument from `testhost/README.md` in an attached shell.
   Record its box/run IDs and wait for `CAPTURE_GATEWAY_READY`. Do not end the
   reservation while builds run: the fixture masks SSH, so only Boat API works.
2. `collect.py configure BOX tmp/verify/config.properties --scope all` privately
   saves that VM's endpoint/token. `run-matrix.sh --build-capture CONFIG` builds
   offbox and pulls the configured APK. Keep all runtime files under ignored
   `tmp/`. Never publish the configured APK.
3. `run-matrix.sh --device APK` allocates through rcsim. Upload the sample APK
   with `runcloud asset push`, then use `cloud-install.py SESSION ASSET` to
   install it on that owned session. Install Orbot similarly for its rows only.
   Record every APK hash. Heartbeat at least every 15 minutes and release the
   session while waiting for long builds. Do not claim an API based on a label.
4. Open `torssh-debug://capture` and accept Android's real VPN consent. The
   capture log reports SDK, ABI, scope, capture UID and sample UID. Reach the
   sample via `torssh-debug://capture?action=sample`; verify its Off state for
   row 1. Run the seeded check with `run-matrix.sh --seed SESSION`. Confirm both
   seeded packet types and a DNS reply, not merely a success log.
5. Use a fresh collector/run per row (or implement and verify bounded slicing).
   Record the row start/end and any fail-closed transition on the packet clock.
   Run row 1 idle for at least 60 seconds. Run the sample's numeric/status debug
   actions for later rows once #7/#8/#9 expose them; do not invent deep-link
   handlers. `runcloud android logs` plus `filter-logs.py` retains allowlisted
   result lines only. Current sample has no scenario deep-link harness yet.
6. `collect.py snapshot BOX tmp/verify/ROW` requests an immutable pcap + bound UID
   sidecar + capture counts. Sequence gaps invalidate completeness. Analyze
   with the exact mode, device IPs `10.237.0.2` / `fd37:37::2`, fixture IPs,
   UID sets, relay/bridge snapshot and transition timestamp for that row. Record
   only redacted results/counts/hashes; pcaps are ignored by git.
7. Stop the VPN and release with `run-matrix.sh --release SESSION`. Delete any
   uploaded fixture assets. Stop the gateway/host reservation, confirm down.sh
   erased onion/SSH state, then `offbox release BOX --delete`. Verify `rcsim list`
   and VM deletion. Never save a snapshot of the fixture or its identities.

Rows 2–4 wait for #7/#8. Rows 5–7 wait for #9; SOCKS mode is measurable, VPN
mode is not. Rows 8–9 additionally need actual device controls and uninterrupted
observation across network changes. Rows 10–11 require process attribution for
shared-UID embedded traffic. Row 12 needs #7 plus the authenticated #3 host.
API 29, API 33 and live 16 KiB-page devices remain unavailable, as recorded in
wiki `device-testing`; this harness does not manufacture those passes.

Lessons from #6's merge gate (2026-11-10, evaluator).

- **Pick the box kind:** `offbox run --base torssh:torssh-skeleton-n01 --git --no-fallback -- …` puts the run on a skeleton-base pool box. A plain run can auto-resume any stopped pool box, including one that holds unread evidence (see Robob #862, bx_2da8dbpm).

- **Long runs:** keep the client attached (a foreground run in a background shell). `--bg` runs whose client goes away can lose their box after about 30 min (Robob #866).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Real process/token/loopback dial probe. Runs with no external interfaces."""
import base64
import copy
import hashlib
import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import secrets
import select
import socket
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
import tempfile
import time

root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
# Assert the exact verified Tor source, not a general assumption about fork/exec.
archive = root / 'third_party/dist/tor-0.4.9.16.tar.gz'
pin = json.loads((root / 'native/sources.json').read_text())[archive.name]['sha256']
assert hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == pin
with tarfile.open(archive) as t:
    source = t.extractfile('tor-0.4.9.16/src/lib/process/process_unix.c').read().decode()
lines = source.splitlines()
assert "Note that we don't close all FDs from here" in lines[225]
assert 'all our open are CLOEXEC' in lines[226]
assert 'execve(argv[0], argv, env->unixoid_environment_block);' in lines[236]
print('PASS pinned Tor process_unix.c:226-228 preserves non-CLOEXEC FDs before execve:237')

exe = sys.argv[1]
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='lyrebird-contract-') as state:
    os.chmod(state, 0o700)
    sentinel = socket.socket()
    sentinel.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0))
    sentinel.listen()
    sentinel.settimeout(0.1)
    target = sentinel.getsockname()
    token = secrets.token_hex(32)
    cert = base64.b64encode(bytes(52)).decode().rstrip('=')
    policy = {'version': 1, 'token': token, 'transport': 'obfs4', 'bridges': [
        {'address': f'{target[0]}:{target[1]}', 'options': {'cert': cert, 'iat-mode': '0'}}]}

    def launch(config, changes=None, raw=None, frame=True, argv=None, inherited=True):
        readfd, writefd = os.pipe()
        env = {'TOR_PT_MANAGED_TRANSPORT_VER': '1', 'TOR_PT_CLIENT_TRANSPORTS': config.get('transport', 'obfs4'),
               'TOR_PT_STATE_LOCATION': state, 'TOR_PT_EXIT_ON_STDIN_CLOSE': '1'}
        env.update(changes or {})
        p = subprocess.Popen([exe, *(argv if argv is not None else [f'--torssh-launch-fd={readfd}'])],
            stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env,
            pass_fds=(readfd,) if inherited else ())
        os.close(readfd)
        try:
            data = json.dumps(config).encode() if raw is None else raw
            if frame and inherited:
                os.write(writefd, struct.pack('!I', len(data)) + data)
        except BrokenPipeError:
            pass
        finally:
            os.close(writefd)
        return p

    def stopped(p, code):
        try:
            stdout, stderr = p.communicate(timeout=7)
            assert p.returncode == code and stdout == b'' and stderr == b'', 'launch refusal'
        finally:
            p.kill()

    bad = copy.deepcopy(policy)
    bad.pop('token')
    stopped(launch(bad), 65)
    bad = copy.deepcopy(policy)
    bad['token'] = 'wrong'
    stopped(launch(bad), 65)
    stopped(launch(policy, inherited=False), 65)
    stopped(launch(policy, frame=False), 65)
    stopped(launch(policy, argv=[]), 64)
    stopped(launch(policy, changes={'TOR_PT_CLIENT_TRANSPORTS': 'obfs4,snowflake'}), 64)

Architecture: `shared/Kafka Cluster.md` §4.2 L99/L105, Registry Deployment §1.4,

## What gets created

Three users on the legacy `kafka-ec2` `scram_users` path, each with a
`crpko/<env>/kafka/scram/<user>` secret and a write-only seed:

- `registry-resync-v1`: 15 literal registry updated.v1 topics, WRITE and DESCRIBE

- `clickhouse-ingestor-canonical-priority-v1`: this branch's 12 runtime topics
  plus the five documented position-bonus topics, each with READ, DESCRIBE and
  DESCRIBE_CONFIGS; 12 runtime groups with READ and DESCRIBE (75 rows).
- `clickhouse-ingestor-canonical-bulk-v1`: 108 runtime topics with the same three
  operations and two runtime groups with READ and DESCRIBE (328 rows).

The three exact secret ARNs are granted through the shared ECS execution policy.
The secret model has execution-role readers only; no task-role grant is added.
Task definitions and the one-off execution role still use broker until SCRAM-2.
The manifest stays pending-security-approval. Without an authorizer, these users
have unrestricted Kafka reach; separate principals alone do not enforce ACLs.
Do not apply or verify ACLs until the separate Phase 3 approval and authorizer work.

## Negative probes

'''

Run these only with the evaluator's apply and upsert authorization. This PR makes
no live AWS or Kafka changes. Retain plan JSON, workflow run IDs and metadata
read-backs. Never read or print secret values.

1. **1a, plan-role deny first.** Dispatch `terraform-dev.yml` with `infra_only=true`,
   `foundationdb_explorer_scope=iam`, `apply=true`. Read
   `crpko-dev-gha-plan/crpko-dev-gha-plan-inline` back with `aws iam get-role-policy`
   using `--profile crpko-dev --region ap-south-1`. For each user, verify one exact
   `...:secret:crpko/dev/kafka/scram/<user>-??????` in
   `DenyKafkaPrincipalSecretRead` and in the encryption-context list of
   `DenyKafkaPrincipalSecretDecrypt`. The pre-apply deny checker blocks secret and
   seed creation if either deny is missing.
2. **1b, create secrets and seeds.** Dispatch the same workflow with
   `infra_only=true`, `foundationdb_explorer_scope=kafka-tls-phase1`, `apply=true`.
   Expect only three secret creates, three seed creates, the upsert document's
   UserName pattern update and the broker node policy's ReadScramSecrets update.
   No execution-role policy or runtime-secrets change belongs in this scope.
   Use `aws secretsmanager describe-secret` for name and KMS key metadata and
   `list-secret-version-ids` to verify AWSCURRENT for each user. The key must be
   the Kafka module's `kms_key_arns["secrets"]` key. The coupling guard requires
   each secret, seed and document pattern together, including no-op rows on retry.
3. **1c, grant injection access.** Dispatch with `infra_only=true`,
   `foundationdb_explorer_scope=kafka-oneoff-scram-grants`, `apply=true`.
   The only change must be an in-place update of
   `module.ecs_runtime.aws_iam_role_policy.execution_kafka_scram_secret[0]`,
   adding exactly the three secret ARNs. Read it back:
   ```bash
   aws iam get-role-policy --profile crpko-dev --region ap-south-1 \\
     --role-name crpko-dev-ecs-execution-role \\
     --policy-name crpko-dev-ecs-execution-kafka-scram
   ```
   Check the exact three ARNs against the metadata from 1b. DecryptKafkaScramSecret
   and all existing reads must be unchanged. This read-back gates SCRAM-2.
4. **2, register credentials.** Run once for each of the three users on broker-1:
   ```bash
   node scripts/runbooks/kafka-scram-user-upsert.mjs --env dev \\
     --profile crpko-dev --region ap-south-1 \\
     --instance-id <broker-1 instance id> --user <user>
   ```
   KRaft replicates the credential. Require terminal Success, response code zero
   and the exact line for each user:
   `SCRAM credential configs for user-principal '<user>' are SCRAM-SHA-512=iterations=8192`.
   On uncertain completion, retain the command ID and inspect that invocation with
   `aws ssm get-command-invocation`; do not resend while it may still run. If no
   command ID was returned, reconcile the existing command before sending again.
   Refresh `plan/kafka/acl-live-snapshot.dev.v1.json`, then run
   `npm run check:kafka-acl-coverage`. None of the three may have the warning
   `is marked existing but has no SCRAM credential on the brokers`.

Only after 1c and 2 pass may SCRAM-2 move definitions and the one-off role, followed
by the canonical runtime refresh and exact running-task read-back. No ACL read-back
runs here: verify mode fails while no authorizer is configured. The separate
Phase 3 program owns ACL apply, authorizer enablement and the probes above.

## Failed seed

A failed local-exec seed is tainted. The guards refuse replacement, so do not
simply rerun or untaint it. With the same authorization as the apply:

1. Read metadata only with `aws secretsmanager list-secret-version-ids`, using
   `--profile crpko-dev --region ap-south-1 --secret-id crpko/dev/kafka/scram/<user>`.
   Count versions tagged AWSCURRENT. One preserves the value; zero means the seed
   will write its first value.
2. Remove only the failed seed from state:
   `terraform -chdir=terraform/roots/dev state rm 'module.kafka_ec2.terraform_data.write_only_seed["<user>"]'`.
   Do not use `terraform untaint`, which keeps the failed instance.
3. Re-plan kafka-tls-phase1. The seed is a first create; the secret and document
   remain no-op or their pending change. The seed writes only when no current value
   exists. Keep all three rows present for the coupling check.

See `balance-bootstrap-kafka-principal.md`, Failed seed, and
`scripts/test-kafka-scram-seed-taint-recovery.mjs` for the real Terraform recovery path.
'''
Path('scripts/runbooks/registry-resync-and-canonical-kafka-principals.md').write_text(header+probes+rollout)
